subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes and continuous batching expectations
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rodriguez <sam@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: pricing & batching follow-up (token volumes, $/1M target)

Hi Sam — great to meet you and Tina on the call today. Thanks for walking through the product use case and the sample traces. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key next steps and a rough pricing sketch so you can validate with finance.

Recap / action items:
- You: share anonymized workload sample (token distribution + concurrency profile) — you mentioned ~1.2M requests/day with a median prompt length ~120 tokens and generation ~80 tokens.
- Us (Redwood): provide a target unit economics estimate and an initial pricing worksheet based on continuous batching.
- Schedule: target decision by end of Aug — you said procurement cycles run 4–6 weeks.

Quick notes on assumptions I used for the worksheet (attached):
- Continuous batching expected (steady stream of small requests, 10–40 tokens input most common).
- Concurrency: bursty peaks to ~300 concurrent requests; steady-state concurrent workers ~40–60.
- Target unit economics: goal is to show price ranges around $X–$Y per 1M tokens (see attached).

Please confirm if the volume estimates below look right so we can finalize the worksheet:
- Monthly tokens (approx): 1.2M requests/day * (120+80)=200 tokens/request => 240M tokens/day => ~7.2B tokens/month (this sounded higher than you expected so double-check).

Attaching our preliminary pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx) and a small template for workload export. I left placeholders where I made guesses.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call if you want to walk the numbers.

Best,
Camila
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: acme-workload-sample.json.gz (compressed)

From: Sam Rodriguez <sam@acme-ai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Patel <tina@acme-ai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & batching follow-up (token volumes, $/1M target)

Thanks Camila — good summary. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Volume: my earlier estimate was sloppy on the daily->monthly math. The 1.2M requests/day was during peak marketing spikes; our baseline is ~250k requests/day. Peak days can go to 1.2M.
- Token distribution: median total tokens/request is ~90 (prompt+response), 95th percentile ~450. So the 200-token average you used is likely high for baseline.
- Concurrency: steady-state 30–50 concurrent, short-lived spikes to 400 for 10–15 minutes during campaigns.
- Budget: procurement has a target TCO for this feature of $8k–15k/month initially (we can expand after product-market fit). That maps to an initial target of roughly $X–$Y per 1M tokens — want to see your numbers here.

I've attached a sanitized 48-hour sample trace (acme-workload-sample.json.gz). Let me know if you want a longer window.

— Sam
Head of Integrations, Acme AI

Attachment: acme-workload-sample.json.gz (compressed)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rodriguez <sam@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & batching follow-up (token volumes, $/1M target)

Thanks for the corrected numbers — that helps a lot. I ran a quick pass against the sample and adjusted assumptions. High level:

- Baseline tokens/day: 250k reqs/day * 90 tokens = ~22.5M tokens/day => ~675M tokens/month.
- Campaign spikes: 1.2M reqs/day * 90 tokens = 108M tokens/day on peak days. If you have ~2–3 campaign days/month that adds ~216–324M tokens/month.
- Combined monthly baseline + campaigns: ~900M–1B tokens/month (plausible given your description).

Unit economics & pricing sketch (continuous batching assumptions):
- Continuous batching reduces per-token cost significantly for steady streams of small requests. For your baseline distribution (median ~90, many small requests), we assume effective batching efficiency yields ~1.8x improvement vs naive per-request serving.
- Concurrency considerations: steady concurrency 30–50 fits our continuous-batching profile; short high spikes to 400 will require temporary burst capacity or fallback to a higher-cost short-term model. We model spikes as 6–10% additional monthly spend if handled with burst capacity.

Initial estimated price bands (ballpark, for discussion):
- Tier A (conservative): $22–$28 per 1M tokens — assumes limited batching gains, some burst-handling premium.
- Tier B (expected): $12–$18 per 1M tokens — assumes continuous batching with good prefix cache hit rates and steady-state concurrency tuning.
- Tier C (aggressive): $6–$10 per 1M tokens — assumes optimized model+quantization, sustained high batching efficiency, and reserved capacity commit.

Mapping to your budget (~$8k–15k/month):
- At Tier B ($12–$18 /1M): $8k/month buys ~444k–666k tokens/month (not sufficient for 900M tokens).
- At Tier C ($6–$10 /1M): $8k/month buys ~800k–1.33M tokens/month (still far below your expected).

Conclusion: to cover ~900M tokens/month within $8k–15k you would need a materially lower $/1M (sub-$1 range) or a reserved capacity commitment / different billing model. Common next steps we see:
- Option 1: start with hosted usage for initial months while you validate product value; then move to a Reserved (Dedicated) plan once token volumes justify a committed rate.
- Option 2: pilot a hybrid where high-volume campaign traffic is routed to dedicated capacity while baseline uses hosted with batching optimizations.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We model two 30-day scenarios with your sample traces (baseline only; baseline + 3 campaign days) and produce a detailed per-token cost breakdown with the assumptions called out.
2) If results look promising, we scope a 3-month Dedicated trial pricing proposal with commit tiers and SLA.

I'll have a short modeling doc and updated worksheet by EOD Wed. Want to loop in finance / solutions (Marissa and Aditya) for the pricing proposal — @Marissa / @Aditya, can one of you take point on a draft committed-tier structure if Sam's team is open?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk the model.

Camila
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (updated)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Rodriguez <sam@acme-ai.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing & batching follow-up (token volumes, $/1M target)

Looping in some suggested committed tiers and quick notes:

- Suggested commit bands (monthly tokens):
  - 500M tokens/month => $9 / 1M tokens (dedicated baseline rate)
  - 1B tokens/month => $6 / 1M tokens
  - 2B+ tokens/month => $4 / 1M tokens + negotiated burst credits

- Pilot recommendation: 90-day pilot with a 3-month lookback for campaign coverage (we credit overage vs commit). Pilot includes:
  - Reserved capacity to cover baseline concurrency (30–50) with burst buffer for 400 spikes (auto-burst to hosted at defined thresholds).
  - Observability: token-level cost dashboard, trace samples, and gating on latency SLOs.

Sam — if you can confirm approx how many campaign days/month and whether campaign traffic can be routed via a separate domain/path, we can model the hybrid pilot.

- Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
